description:
People often ask Matt how to make their voice heard. Well, that's the wrong question.

In this Quick Thinks episode of the Think Fast, Talk Smart podcast, host Matt Abrahams treats speaking louder as a trainable skill rather than an innate gift. Over nine minutes, Matt Abrahams runs a complete diagnostic on voice training and core communication skills, borrowing from the stage, the running track, and the sound booth to optimize your fuel source, delivery system, and equipment. In this Think Fast, Talk Smart episode with Matt Abrahams, discover practical public speaking tips, such as:
• The place most people breathe from when they're nervous is exactly the place that kills their volume.
• A one-word shift in mindset (borrowed from acting) that changes how loud and how open your body becomes when you speak.
• Vocal stamina works exactly like training for a race. And the "treadmill" is already lying around in your house.
• The hidden A lavalier mic rule that quietly drops your volume if you break it.
• A body-positioning trick that Matt recommends ONLY for Handheld mics and nothing else.

Most people don't need more confidence to be heard but better breath support and a clearer understanding of how to use a microphone. Breath, posture, stamina, and microphones are four different tools, BUT the decision in all cases stays the same: where you WANT your voice to land before you open your mouth.

About Matt
Matt Abrahams is a leading communication expert, lecturer in organizational behavior at Stanford GSB, and host of the award-winning Think Fast, Talk Smart podcast. He has coached presenters at TED, the World Economic Forum, and the UN Secretary-General's office, and his online talks have garnered millions of views worldwide. He is the author of Think Faster, Talk Smarter and Speaking Up without Freaking Out, two bestselling guides to confident, spontaneous communication.

Key Quotes
• "Your voice is a wind instrument. The more you do with it, the more your volume and voice can be affected by it." - Matt Abrahams (00:56) 
• "Lower, slower breathing gives you more vocal support so you can project your voice." - Matt Abrahams (02:45)
• "It's not about broadcasting it out. It's about focusing on placing your voice in a certain space." - Matt Abrahams (03:42)
• "Reading out loud to build vocal stamina is like running on a treadmill to build your stamina for running a road race." - Matt Abrahams (4:54)
• "You want to make sure that you have the energy at the end of your communication as well as at the beginning." - Matt Abrahams (05:16)
